_note: VOX-033 gate set. Ten queries: 8 answerable with an expected source file:page, 2 deliberately
absent from the corpus. Scored by tests/gates/gate_poc_pdf.py — correct-source@3 over the 8,
refusal rate over the 2. Run with: make gate-poc
Dev only. evals/heldout/ is sealed as heldout-v1 and holds zero document queries (its
categories are greet / entity / ambig / escalate / refuse); it is not reopened for this. So
every number scored off this file was computed on queries the Builder can read, and nothing
here bounds how much the implementation was shaped by these ten cases. The gate prints that
limit next to the numbers rather than leaving it in a design doc.
NOT the floor-calibration set. That is retrieval_floor_queries.json, and none of its 7 hits or
6 misses appear here — those thirteen are what RETRIEVAL_SCORE_FLOOR = 0.28 was fitted to, and
a gate scored on them measures how well the floor was fitted, which is a number that can only
go up and cannot be wrong.
expect is a list because two of these answers really are printed in more than one place: the PL
encashment rule is stated verbatim on separation-policy p13 and again on p26. It is a list for
that reason only, never to widen a label until retrieval clears it.
Every expect label was read off the actual chunk in runs/chunks.jsonl before it was written
here, and two candidate queries were cut for failing that check rather than relabelled: 'can I
accept a gift from a vendor' (retrieval missed it, but 'gift' appears in 5 chunks — the corpus
does cover it, so it is not an absent query) and 'who pays for my hotel stay on official
travel' (travel-policy has no accommodation section; 'hotel' appears only incidentally, so it
is not an answerable one). retrieval_floor_queries.json records two labels that were written
wrong first for the same reason. Label error is the one failure mode that fails this gate for
nothing.
q03 is expected to miss, and it is in the set on purpose. It is the STT-damaged form of q02 —
ARCHITECTURE.md records the live turn where 'leave encashment' came back from Whisper as
'leaving cashment', destroying the one high-information term before retrieval ran. Retrieval
returns leave-policy p7/p10 (leave accrual arithmetic) instead of the separation-policy pages
that hold the rule. The floor of 7/8 is set to allow exactly this one: seven clean queries pass
and the known-damaged one does not. A regression on any clean query drops it to 6/8 and fails.
The two absent queries take the two different refusal paths on purpose, because src/answer.py
distinguishes them and only one of them involves a model at all: q09 clears the floor (it
retrieves leave-policy chunks about other leave types) and must be refused by the model from
excerpts that do not contain the answer; q10 is rejected by the floor, so it is refused with no
model call. Both are HR-shaped and share corpus vocabulary — 'leave', 'days', 'company',
'employee', 'coverage' — because a miss written in unrelated words would clear any floor and
prove nothing. Neither subject appears anywhere in the corpus: grep -ic over runs/chunks.jsonl
returns 0 for 'menstrual' and 0 for 'health insurance|mediclaim|medical insurance'.

answerable.q: how many paternity leaves am I entitled to according to policy
answerable.why: ARCHITECTURE.md's worked paternity case. The entitlement is on p12; p14 carries only the terms and conditions, so the label stays narrow.

answerable.q: how is my privilege leave encashment calculated when I leave the company
answerable.why: The rule lives in separation-policy, not leave-policy — the trap this set exists to catch. Stated verbatim on both pages, hence two labels. Answers by stating the formula, which is what answer_from_source_v2.md asks for instead of computing it.

answerable.q: how much my leaving cashment would be
answerable.why: q02 as Whisper actually transcribed it in a live turn. Expected to miss: retrieval returns leave-policy p7/p10. This is the one query the 7/8 floor allows to fail, and it is a measurement of STT damage, not of retrieval.

answerable.q: what are the standard office working hours and shift timings
answerable.why: The answer is nothing but figures — 8 hours, 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM, 40 weekly hours — so it exercises answer.ungrounded_numbers() on a reply that must be allowed to say numbers.

answerable.q: how many maternity leaves does a woman employee get
answerable.why: A clean single-page answer in the largest document. The control: if this one fails, the index itself is wrong.

answerable.q: what is the dress code in the office
answerable.why: Retrieval ranks the right page third — p12 (Remote Work Etiquette) and annual-event-policy p3 outrank it. The query that justifies measuring @3 rather than @1.

answerable.q: what happens to my laptop if I resign before two years of allotment
answerable.why: A conditional answer rather than a lookup — the condition (before 2 years) changes the outcome, so a reply that ignores it is wrong while still citing the right page.

answerable.q: how often does the performance appraisal cycle happen
answerable.why: A seventh document in the set, and the answer is a duration rather than a count.

absent.q: how many days of paid menstrual leave does the company give
absent.why: Clears the floor on leave-policy chunks about casual, privilege and leave-without-pay, none of which mention it. The model has to refuse from excerpts that look relevant — the refusal path that costs a free-tier call and is the one that can fabricate.

absent.q: what is the health insurance coverage amount for my family
absent.why: Rejected by the floor: best unfloored score 0.159 on leave-policy p25 (compensation during leave without pay). Refused with no model call at all, so it tests RETRIEVAL_SCORE_FLOOR rather than the prompt.
